reason: Open Library search inside both Hallo scans shows the wording before the Indices heading. The Holt, Rinehart and Winston 1971 scan (starofredemption0000rose, leaf 474) reads: Whither, then, do the wings of the gate open? Thou knowest it not? INTO LIFE. The Beacon 1972 scan (starofredemption0000rose_a1a6) reads the same. Santner and Ricoeur (Figuring the Sacred) both cite the line to p. 424, and Maybaum, Samuelson, Bolle and Cohen quote the same wording. It is the Hallo wording to the letter. Other renderings exist: the Blue Guide’s Where do the wings of the gate open? Do you not know? and Trepp’s whereto ... Unto Life. The card has not drifted toward either. The terminal full stop is the one liberty: the Hallo OCR shows none after LIFE, which ends the book, while the German has one (INS LEBEN.). Rule 6 needs a stop, and several reprints of Hallo print one (Martin 1969, Religion and the Authority of the Past). The line is Rosenzweig’s own sentence, not scripture: the Micah words stand just before it, outside the quotation. So it is in scope as philosophy. shipped.js: not shipped, no near opening, Rosenzweig at 0 of 3, not banned. The source line is 119 characters with no dash and leads with the name. Philosophy is the right tag. It is the book’s closing line, so the fame holds, and it opens onto life, which is December. Suggested note, not a refutation: say the book ends at LIFE and the full stop is the German’s.
